data.name: World Truck Racing
data.detailed_description:
Enter the world of Truck Racing in a new arcade-racing game. Sit behind the wheel of monsters with over 4000 hp engines allowing them to accelerate just as fast as supercars.
Test your skills in close-contact sport. Drive fast and find your way between opponent cars to the first place. Adjust your car's settings to achieve handling and performance fitted to one of 16 racetracks around the world.

Game features:
  • arcade-style driving system
  • 12 racing trucks in 2 classes
  • 16 race tracks based on actual locations around the world
  • visual and mechanical car tuning
  • 4 racing modes

reviews.review:
I decided to buy this game despite the mostly negative review score because I was looking for an arcade semi-truck racing game and there weren't many such games on Steam at the time I bought it. Even now most of the semi-truck games focus on transporting stuff and the racing ones are mostly simulations. To be honest it's not as bad as the review score, or the reviews ..sorry but I couldn't figure out why people hate the game due to the lack of any constructive criticism.

World Truck Tracing could be described as an arcade racing game with a simulation aesthetic. The races take place in tracks that are based on real circruits and while they are obviously not a 1:1 resemblance, I found the overall level design pretty good.  What's impressive is the amount of details outside of the main layout too. The level designer made sure that the world out of the track doesn't feel empty. Apart from buildings, trees and billboards there are also parks with rollercoasters and ferris wheels. I also like the variety of colors. The spectators are easy to miss as they are tiny sprites, but at least you can hear them.

The career mode features 15 championships in which 70 race events are distributed. Some events can feel repetitive because there are 15 tracks in total ( store page says 16, might be a typo ), but to add some variety we get to play the tracks on different weather conditions. I found it a little funny that they added practice and qualifying sessions, I mean you don't get a penalty for cutting the track, hitting penalty markers ( yes, there are penalty markers too ) or colliding with other drivers so who cares. Beating the AI is easy even when you start from last place. Another funny thing is that you can basically use the pits as a shortcut in some circuits. Like, there is no pit stop. You just casually drive through there. They do however repair any damage that was done to the truck. My guess is that these things exist to give that simulation feeling.

Negatives :

- The B class truck sounds like an old pickup truck and not like a semi truck.

- Unlocking new trucks is bugged. I think they are supposed to unlock once you beat a certain amount of championships, but all trucks remain locked even after completing the game. 

- Continuing to the next championship is sometimes bugged, requires a fix that involves editing the game's registry file.

- Music is good but you can't hear it. There is no volume slider for just the music. 

Overall I'd say it is worth the asking price. Keep in mind that this game was made by only 4 people, one of them solely working on sounds and music and the other being a project manager. So basically 1 guy did all the programming and the other one all the 3D stuff ( trucks, levels etc. ).
